extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters) involved in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for handling amendments, reopening prosecution, issuance of Right of Appeal Notices (RAN), panel review, and appeals in inter partes reexamination proceedings under the MPEP and relevant CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of proposed amendments after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner cannot, as a matter of right, amend claims rejected in the ACP, add new claims after an ACP, nor reinstate previously canceled claims. A showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) is required and will be evaluated by the examiner for all proposed amendments after the ACP, except where an amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner’s suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or in some other way requires only a cursory review by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entry of the proposed amendment would withdraw a ground of rejection or indicate any additional claim as patentable, the amendment generally raises new issues and the examiner is not required to enter it. Examiner should consider feasibility of entry where the entirety of the amendment results only in an additional claim being indicated as patentable and is encouraged to enter such an amendment unless entry would cause an 'undue burden.' If not entered, the examiner should explain the 'undue burden.' Multiple amendments submitted after ACP: only the first will be considered for entry; others are returned as improper. An amendment filed after the RAN will not be entered absent a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183; to accept an amendment after the RAN, the examiner can reopen prosecution, enter the amendment, and issue a new ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must explain reasons for not entering amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a proposed amendment is not entered, the examiner will provide a detailed explanation of the reasons for not entering the proposed amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amended claims present a new issue requiring further consideration or search, the new issue should be identified and an explanation provided as to why a new search is necessary and/or why more than nominal consideration is necessary. The RAN or Office action should also identify which submissions after the ACP have been entered and considered, and which have not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reopening of prosecution when examiner changes position
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission after ACP has been filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.951 and the examiner decides to modify his/her position, the examiner should ordinarily reopen prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A RAN cannot be issued until the patent owner has had the opportunity to address each and every rejection prior to the appeal stage. Thus, prosecution should be reopened where any new ground of rejection is made or any additional claim is rejected. Reopening is ordinarily done by issuing a non-ACP Office action prior to the ACP stage. Reopening is not required when a new finding of patentability is made (i.e., a ground withdrawn or claim indicated patentable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary reopening of prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to mandatory situations, the examiner should be liberal in reopening prosecution where the equities of the situation make such reopening appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an amendment after ACP would make at least one claim patentable except for one or two minor changes that could be easily corrected, the examiner should reopen prosecution (since interviews are not permitted and other mechanisms are unavailable) and issue a new ACP suggesting the amendment. Examiner should consider whether reopening would create an 'undue burden' on the Office before declining to reopen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and content requirements of Right of Appeal Notice (RAN)
rubrics_metrics.description: A RAN is a final Office action under 37 CFR 1.953 comprising a final rejection and/or final decision favorable to patentability and must identify the status of each claim and set a one-month time period for either party to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAN must (A) set forth grounds of rejection for all claims rejected, (B) state reasons why a proposed rejection is not made for decisions favorable to patentability when contested by third party requester, and (C) state reasons for patentability for claims 'allowed' and not contested. The RAN should restate relied-upon grounds/findings and set forth reasons in detail so parties can judge the advisability of filing an appeal. No amendment can be made in response to a RAN; no affidavit or other evidence can be submitted after RAN except as provided in 37 CFR 1.981 or 41.77(b)(1). Use form PTOL-2066 as cover sheet and conclude with form paragraph 26.08 advising parties of appeal rights and paragraph 26.73 for correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited Right of Appeal Notice (expedited RAN) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after the patent owner’s response to the initial Office action on the merits, the patent owner and all third party requesters may stipulate that the issues are appropriate for a final action and request issuance of an expedited RAN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must (A) stipulate issues are appropriate for final action, (B) have concurrence of patent owner and all third party requesters, (C) identify all appealable issues, and (D) identify and discuss positions of the patent owner and third party requester(s) on those issues. If the examiner determines no other issues are present or should be raised, a RAN limited to the identified issues will be issued. If other issues need to be raised, the examiner should deny the request. The request does not extend time for any response/comments due when the request is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference prior to issuing RAN
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a RAN, the examiner will inform the CRU SPE or TC QAS of intent to issue the action; the CRU SPE/TC QAS will convene a panel review conference to review patentability pursuant to MPEP § 2671.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the proposed RAN shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two other conferees initialing the action. If the conference does not confirm the treatment, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to request entry of amendment (37 CFR 1.181) and related petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment submitted after the ACP has not been entered because it does not comply with 37 CFR 1.116, the patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting entry of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be filed within the time period for filing a notice of appeal or cross appeal. Filing a 1.181 petition does not toll the time for filing a notice of appeal; patent owner is encouraged also to file (1) a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 requesting waiver of the prohibition on extending time for filing an appeal brief (37 CFR 41.66(a)), and (2) a request for extension of the period to file the appeal brief until after a decision on the 1.181 petition. The third party requester may once file comments responsive to the 1.181 petition within 30 days of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on amendments and evidence after RAN and after filing an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.116(d)(1) states that no amendment other than canceling claims (where such cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims) can be made after the RAN in an inter partes reexamination except as provided by 37 CFR 1.981 or 41.77(b)(1). 37 CFR 1.116(f) bars affidavits or other evidence after the RAN except as provided. After filing an appeal (37 CFR 41.63), only certain canceling amendments and limited other submissions may be admitted under narrow reopening provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed after the RAN will not be entered absent a grantable 1.183 petition. After the date of filing an appeal, amendments canceling claims may be admitted (37 CFR 41.63(a)) where cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims; other amendments and affidavits/declarations/exhibits filed after appeal generally will not be admitted except as permitted by reopening prosecution under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal timing, notice of appeal content, and procedural requirements (37 CFR 41.61 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of a RAN, the owner and requester have one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) to file a notice of appeal to the Board; the notice must identify the appealed claim(s), be signed by the party or authorized representative, and be accompanied by the fee. Time periods for filing notice of appeal or cross appeal may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal must be taken from all the rejections (for owner) or all determinations favorable to patentability (for requester) which the appealing party proposes to contest. If a notice of appeal or cross appeal is timely filed but defective, appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time to file an amended notice; failure to correct will result in dismissal. If notice of appeal filed before RAN, it will be placed in the file but not considered. Forms (e.g., PTOL-2067) should be used for notifications of defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-appeal rules and timing (multiple parties and sequencing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who has not filed a notice of appeal may file a notice of cross appeal within fourteen days of service of an opposing party’s notice of appeal (37 CFR 41.61(b)). Where there are multiple third-party requesters in a merged proceeding, special timing rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than two parties exist, a third party cross appeal must be filed within fourteen days of service of a patent owner’s notice of appeal. Cross appeal is available only from a 'notice of appeal' (not from a 'notice of cross appeal'), so sequencing matters: if a patent owner files a notice of cross appeal after the original appeal period but within fourteen days of a requester’s appeal, the second requester may be barred from cross-appealing if the original appeal period has expired. Cross appeal content mirrors notice of appeal but must be titled as such. Defective cross appeals may be corrected within a non-extendable period of one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant brief timing and content requirements (37 CFR 41.66–41.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must be filed no later than two months from the latest filing date of the last-filed notice of appeal or cross appeal (37 CFR 41.66). The brief must be signed, accompanied by the requisite fee, and contain specified items under appropriate headings in a prescribed order (37 CFR 41.67).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file an appellant’s brief with the fee within the time allowed will result in dismissal of that appellant’s appeal. The brief must be served on all other parties in accordance with § 1.903 and include items such as identification of the real party in interest (and other items listed in 41.67(c)(1)(i)–(xi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requester estoppel (35 U.S.C. 315(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party requester whose inter partes reexamination request results in an order under section 313 is estopped from asserting in later civil actions the invalidity of any claim finally determined to be valid and patentable on any ground which the requester raised or could have raised during the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This estoppel does not prevent assertion of invalidity based on newly discovered prior art unavailable to the requester and the Office at the time of the reexamination proceedings. Examiners and deciding officials should be mindful of this when considering petitions and decisions.
